events.title: The Second Council of Lyons opens
events.shortBlurb: The fourteenth ecumenical council gathered to seek reunion with the Greeks and reform of the Church…
body: On 7 May 1274 Pope Gregory X opened the Second Council of Lyons, the fourteenth ecumenical council, attended by hundreds of bishops and by envoys of the Byzantine emperor. Its chief aims were the reunion of the Eastern and Western Churches, aid for the Holy Land, and the reform of morals and clergy.

At the council a formula of reunion with the Greek Church was solemnly proclaimed, though it proved short-lived. The gathering also set rules for future papal elections. St. Thomas Aquinas died on his way to the council, and St. Bonaventure, who took a leading part in it, died at Lyons before it closed.
